client.name: Scottsdale Med Spa Outreach
client.description: Scottsdale-area independent med spas, aesthetics clinics, and IV therapy practices. High-LTV, brand-conscious owners whose websites are typically the booking bottleneck.

icp.q_keywords: med spa OR medical spa OR aesthetics OR cosmetic OR botox OR injectables OR laser OR microneedling OR IV therapy

qualification.business_description: a website conversion consultancy that helps independent med spas turn Instagram and Google Maps traffic into booked appointments by fixing technical issues on their sites — page speed, booking flow friction, missing local SEO schema, photo quality. Not an AI agency, not a generic web design shop — narrowly focused on conversion-rate fixes for med spa booking funnels.
qualification.pain_point_lens: could be fixed with website conversion-rate work — slow mobile site, broken/clunky booking flow, missing LocalBusiness schema, low-res or unoptimized photos, no IG-to-site continuity, weak above-the-fold hero. Do NOT include AI-related pain points (no AI follow-up, no AI scheduling, no chatbot pain points)
qualification.ideal_customer_description: An independent Scottsdale-area med spa or aesthetics clinic with 2-30 staff, founder-led or with a small leadership team. Typically does $800K-3M in revenue. Owner is the lead practitioner, cares deeply about brand, and runs a heavy Instagram presence. Bookings come through their website and IG link-in-bio. Site is usually a basic Wix/Squarespace template that doesn't reflect the polish of the brand and has measurable issues (slow mobile load, broken booking flow, low-res photos, missing schema markup). Decision-maker is a single owner-practitioner — fast close, no committee.
qualification.service_focus: A complete website rebuild that makes their site as polished as their brand and Instagram, plus monthly conversion optimization (booking flow, schema for Google Maps, page speed, before/after gallery). Tied directly to bookings/revenue, not vanity metrics. NEVER mention AI tools, AI follow-up sequences, AI rebooking, AI scheduling, or any AI-related service. The pitch is purely site/conversion.

email.tone: peer auditor, not salesperson — speak like another practice owner who happens to know web/conversion. Casual, observational, not pitchy.
email.cta_style: soft — offer a 2-minute Loom audit only, not a discovery call

openers: Was looking at [Company]'s site this morning and noticed [observation]...
Hey — quick note on [Company]. The [specific element] on your site is [issue]...
Took a quick look at [Company] this week. One thing stood out: [issue]...
wedges: mobile page-speed angle — cite '53% of mobile users abandon sites that take more than 3 seconds to load' (Think with Google) or Google's Core Web Vitals threshold (LCP under 2.5 seconds for 'good')
booking flow friction angle — cite that 'each additional step in a mobile booking flow drops completion by ~10%' (industry research, NOT Google)

schema markup / Google Maps visibility angle — cite 'pages with LocalBusiness schema render rich Google Maps results — without it, your listing competes with text-only entries' (Google Search Central guidance, no percentage)
photo quality / page weight angle — cite 'Google's mobile-first index downranks pages where the largest image takes longer than 2.5 seconds to load' (Core Web Vitals LCP)
hero / above-the-fold angle — cite Google's research that mobile users decide whether to stay or leave within 3 seconds based on the above-the-fold experience
ctas: Want me to send it over?
Reply 'send it' and I'll have it to you tomorrow.
Yes or no on the walkthrough?
Happy to send if it sounds useful.

email.value_proposition_line: Briefly mention you can put together a 2-minute Loom walking through the issue and a couple more — this is the value, not a meeting or a free site. Vary the exact phrasing — do not say 'I put together a 2-minute Loom' verbatim every email; sometimes say 'I can record a quick walkthrough', 'happy to film a 2-min audit', 'can send a Loom showing it', etc.
email.cta_line: Close with the EXACT CTA phrasing assigned in the ROTATION ASSIGNMENT block. DO NOT include any Calendly link, calendar URL, booking link, or phone number anywhere in the body.
custom_guidelines: DO NOT mention AI, AI tools, AI follow-up, AI rebooking, AI scheduling, automation, chatbots, or any AI-related service anywhere in the email. The entire pitch is about website conversion fixes — nothing else.
DO NOT use phrases like 'I hope this email finds you well', 'Just wanted to reach out', 'circling back', 'I'd love to', or 'happy to'.
DO NOT mention 'building you a free website', 'I built a demo', 'free audit report', or any pre-built site offer — this is a Loom pitch, not a free-site pitch.
If the prospect's first name is blank, do NOT use 'Hi [blank]' or invent a name. Lead straight into the observation.
PICK EXACTLY ONE pain point from the list and build the email around that ONE issue. Do NOT list multiple issues in the body.
Only mention Instagram if the assigned wedge specifically calls for it — do NOT default to 'Instagram vs site mismatch' framing.
Mention 'a few other AZ med spas' in passing only if it fits naturally — do not force it into every email.
Sign-off should be just 'Vince' or '— Vince' — never 'Vincent Kalman, Founder of Jontri Consulting'.

Subject line MUST be unique across the campaign. Under 5 words, lowercase, hints at the specific observation. AVOID generic templates like 'quick note on your site' or 'your booking flow' that other emails will collide with. Examples of varied formats: 'something on [domain]', '[company] — your hero', 'mobile load on [company]', 'your maps listing', '[company] booking', '3 seconds on [domain]'. Use the company name or domain in roughly half of subjects to make them feel unique.

The body MUST be at least 60 words and no more than 130 words. Never output an empty or near-empty body. If you find yourself writing fewer than 60 words, expand the observation with one more sentence of context.
